name: Saint Jerome
history: The greatest biblical scholar of the early Church. A brilliant, prickly priest from Dalmatia, he learned Hebrew in the Syrian desert, served Pope Damasus in Rome, and spent his last thirty-four years in Bethlehem translating the Scriptures into Latin. His Vulgate was the Bible of the Western Church for more than a thousand years.
life: Jerome was born at Stridon, on the borders of Dalmatia, and studied in Rome, where he was baptised. A great lover of the pagan classics, he later told of a dream in which he was judged a Ciceronian rather than a Christian. He tried the hermit’s life in the desert of Chalcis and there learned Hebrew from a Jewish convert. Ordained priest at Antioch, he came to Rome in 382 and became secretary to Pope Damasus, who asked him to revise the Latin Gospels. There he guided a circle of devout Roman women, among them Paula and her daughter Eustochium. After Damasus died he left for the Holy Land, and from 386 lived at Bethlehem, where Paula built monasteries for men and women. He translated most of the Old Testament from the Hebrew, wrote commentaries and letters, and quarrelled fiercely with his critics. He died at Bethlehem in 420.
prayerTo: Saint Jerome, you gave your life to the word of God and fought your own fierce temper all your days. Pray for translators, scholars and all who teach the Scriptures, and for me, that I may read the Bible daily, love it as you did, and bring my faults humbly to the Lord. Amen.
penance: Read a chapter of the Bible slowly today, perhaps a Gospel or a psalm, and hold back the sharp word when you are tempted to speak it.
meditation: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ. How well do you know the Gospels, and how could you come to know them better?
prayer: O God, Who graciously gave Your Church blessed Jerome, Your Confessor and peerless teacher, to explain the Holy Scriptures, grant, we beseech You, that, with the help of his merits and by Your assistance, we may be able to put into practice what he has taught us by his life and works. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
